proposed_comments.title: Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

confidence.rationale: The pinned call graph reaches WinRT globalization before sanitization, and the new sanitizer uses WinRT JSON without an apartment initialized in wmain.

proposed_comments.body:
### Initialize WinRT before BugReportTool uses it

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `ReportWindowsSettings` and the `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` call in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** `wmain` calls `ReportWindowsSettings` before sanitization, and that function uses C++/WinRT globalization APIs. The pinned `wmain` path does not initialize a WinRT apartment, so those calls can fail before the report is packaged; the sanitizer's WinRT JSON parsing also depends on the same thread's apartment.

**Why it matters:** A report that should be collected and sanitized can instead stop before a ZIP is produced.

**Suggested change:** Initialize a WinRT apartment at the beginning of `wmain`, before `ReportWindowsSettings` or any other WinRT caller, and pair it with scope-bound `winrt::uninit_apartment()`. Keep the existing fail-closed behavior if initialization or sanitization fails.

**Verification:** The exact-head source trace shows `ReportWindowsSettings` is called at `Main.cpp:374` before `sanitize_report` at line 406, and its body invokes WinRT globalization APIs. The exact-upstream candidate built, and all nine focused privacy tests passed; those tests do not exercise BugReportTool's `wmain` at runtime.

proposed_comments.title: Skip writes when a JSON document needs no redaction

confidence.rationale: The pinned function returns success without changing valid unchanged JSON, then unconditionally opens the file with truncation; the candidate regression test passes.

proposed_comments.body:
### Skip writes when a JSON document needs no redaction

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `diagnostic_privacy::redact_security_keys` and the `.json` write in `sanitize_report` in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/DiagnosticPrivacy.h`.

**Problem:** A valid JSON document with no sensitive key makes `redact_security_keys` return `true` without changing `contents`, but `sanitize_report` still opens the file with `std::ios::trunc` and rewrites it.

**Why it matters:** An unchanged JSON file that is readable but not writable can make sanitization throw and prevent creation of the entire report archive; needless serialization can also alter formatting without privacy benefit.

**Suggested change:** Have the redaction routine report whether the document changed separately from parse success, and skip opening the output stream when it did not. Add a regression test for valid unchanged JSON without write access.

**Verification:** The exact-head source trace shows the unconditional output open after a successful parse. On the exact-upstream candidate, the no-write-access regression test and all nine `DiagnosticPrivacyTests` passed. This is a source-path conclusion; no baseline end-to-end report was produced.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve the cause when sanitization aborts

confidence.rationale: The catch-all visibly discards typed exceptions from a sanitizer that configures streams to throw and invokes WinRT; candidate typed diagnostics compile.

proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve the cause when sanitization aborts

**Severity:** `low`

**Affected code:** The catch-all around `diagnostic_privacy::sanitize_report` in `tools/BugReportTool/BugReportTool/Main.cpp`.

**Problem:** The catch-all discards the exception and prints the same message for every sanitization failure, including stream failures and WinRT errors.

**Why it matters:** Users cannot distinguish a file-access problem from a JSON/WinRT failure when the report ZIP is not created, which makes the failure harder to diagnose.

**Suggested change:** Catch `winrt::hresult_error` and `std::exception` before the catch-all, write the HRESULT/message or `what()` to stderr, retain a generic fallback for unknown exceptions, and keep the current cleanup and failure return.

**Verification:** The pinned sanitizer configures streams to throw on I/O failure and uses WinRT JSON parsing; the exact-upstream candidate build passed. No end-to-end report failure was invoked.
